name: wafw00f
summary: Identify and fingerprint Web Application Firewall (WAF) products protecting a website.
highlights: -v — Enable verbosity, multiple -v options increase verbosity
-a — Find all WAFs which match the signatures, do not stop testing on the first one
-r — Do not follow redirections given by 3xx responses
-t — Test for one specific WAF (use --list to get names, quote names with spaces e.g. "AireeCDN
-o — Write output to csv, json or text file depending on file extension. For stdout, specify -
-f — Force output format to csv, json or text.
-i — Read targets from a file. Input format can be csv, json or text. For csv and json, a `url`
-l — List all WAFs that WAFW00F is able to detect

flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: --verbose
flags.description: Enable verbosity, multiple -v options increase verbosity

flags.name: --findall
flags.description: Find all WAFs which match the signatures, do not stop testing on the first one

flags.name: --noredirect
flags.description: Do not follow redirections given by 3xx responses

flags.name: --test
flags.description: Test for one specific WAF (use --list to get names, quote names with spaces e.g. "AireeCDN (Airee)")

flags.name: --output
flags.description: Write output to csv, json or text file depending on file extension. For stdout, specify - as filename.

flags.name: --format
flags.description: Force output format to csv, json or text.

flags.name: --input-file

flags.name: --proxy
flags.description: Use an HTTP proxy to perform requests, examples: http://hostname:8080, socks5://hostname:1080, http://user:pass@hostname:8080

flags.name: --version
flags.description: Print out the current version of WafW00f and exit.

flags.name: --headers
flags.description: Pass custom headers via a text file to overwrite the default header set.

flags.name: --timeout
flags.description: Set the timeout for the requests.

examples.explanation: Check if a website is using any WAF
Test for all detectable WAFs without stopping at the first match
Pass requests through a proxy (such as BurpSuite)
Test for a specific WAF product (run `wafw00f --list` to get list of all supported WAFs)
Pass custom headers from a file
List all WAFs that can be detected
